source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on and boot in BIOS.
2. Change all/random setting to non-default in this BIOS function.
3. Save and reboot.
4. Boot in to BIOS and  check your setting still exist.
5. Press load default,save and reboot.
6. Boot in to BIOS,setting in this function should match the SPEC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error log happen.
2. Normal reboot ,no hang、crash happen.
3. Check your setting still exist.
4. The default setting should matches SPEC."

original_test_intent: Verify that approved TLS authentication firmware values persist across save/reboot and return to SPEC defaults after Load Default without weakening trust, exposing secrets or losing the intended management endpoint.
original_method: Change TLS Auth Configuration fields in BIOS, save/reboot and verify persistence; then Load Default, save/reboot and compare with SPEC while verifying the approved management endpoint and preserving secret confidentiality.
manual_activity: A human must operate the firmware TLS Auth page, approve any trust/credential selection, execute both save/reboot/default phases and inspect settings. Endpoint validation is supporting evidence only.
required_inputs: Named TLS/auth fields with baseline, non-default and SPEC-default values
Approved endpoint, protocol, hostname and trust-chain model
Certificate roles and credential owner without secret disclosure
Console/operator, secure credential handling and alternate management/OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Never operationalize all/random or use unvalidated production trust/credentials.
Do not record private keys, passwords, tokens or recoverable secrets in commands, screenshots, logs or evidence.
Maintain an independent management/recovery path before changing authentication.
Stop on certificate ambiguity, downgrade, wrong endpoint, authentication or management loss.
Restore the approved final trust state.
agent_execution_scope: Collect redacted certificate metadata, protocol/endpoint validation, reachability and BMC health evidence when approved.
Compare operator firmware captures and redacted endpoint results against the matrix.
Do not drive BIOS, reveal secrets, select trust anchors, bypass validation or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Define/approve TLS fields/defaults, trust model, credential handling and recovery.
Perform/capture persistence and default-restoration phases with secrets excluded.
Evaluate firmware and secure endpoint evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly rejects agent BIOS execution. No source command exists; endpoint/TLS tools may validate only the approved endpoint using redacted output and cannot replace the firmware UI.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain manual BIOS changes and use approved endpoint/TLS verification limited to protocol and certificate metadata; never pass secrets on visible command lines or dump key material.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source two-phase sequence, no-script state and 5/20-minute fields are preserved; all/random remains source text but cannot authorize security changes.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map each approved firmware field to endpoint, protocol, certificate role, trust expectation and recovery path; capture redacted firmware/endpoint evidence at baseline, persistence, default restoration and final state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact firmware TLS-auth implementation and approved management service.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, endpoint/service and TLS verification-tool versions without exposing secrets.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform TLS Auth Configuration specification and project PKI/authentication policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds trust-path identity, secret-redaction and lockout recovery while preserving both firmware transitions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; certificate metadata/handshake evidence does not claim private-key or credential correctness beyond the approved authentication check.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field/default matrix, endpoint/trust model, credential owner and rollback.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A successful connection can still target the wrong endpoint; hostname, chain and intended service identity must all be bound.

project_override_considerations: The project selects the endpoint, trust anchors and authentication method. Results apply only to that named path and must not claim broader PKI or cipher coverage unless explicitly planned.
expected_evidence: Identity, approval, redacted trust/endpoint baseline and alternate recovery
First save/reboot persistence plus redacted endpoint/authentication evidence
Load Default, second save/reboot, SPEC comparison and secure management health
Final trust/auth state, secret-leak check and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require persistence and default restoration. Missing trust, endpoint and credential specifics are readiness inputs, not source contradictions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The TLS setting lifecycle is clear. Security inputs and alternate recovery gate execution but do not permanently block the library case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees with manual classification and adds endpoint/trust/secret safety.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its strong TLS controls and endpoint evidence but rejects PARTIAL based solely on supporting automation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Restores MANUAL ONLY and explicitly separates redacted tool results from engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents credential leakage or management lockout and prevents an automated handshake from being mistaken for automated firmware acceptance.
independent_technical_reasoning: Human firmware interaction and visual persistence/default checks remain the core acceptance, so MANUAL ONLY applies. Automated TLS checks are supportive and must remain secret-safe.
no_automatic_retry: Do not repeat authentication changes, login attempts, reboot or default load after lockout, trust ambiguity or management loss; preserve redacted evidence and obtain engineer disposition.
